newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rhone-Poulenc Rorer sees innovation boost profit.
newsitem.headline: Rhone-Poulenc Rorer sees innovation boost profit.

text.p: Rhone-Poulenc Rorer, the U.S. based pharmaceutical subsidiary of Rhone-Poulenc SA, said on Tuesday it expected product innovation to boost its earnings per share by more than 10 percent by the year 2000.

Michel de Rosen, executive chairman, told a news conference that the group wanted to be market leader in five of its therapeutic fields -- cancer, cardio vascular, asthma, anti-inflammatory and plasma proteins.

"We are not preparing a big deal for 1996 but we are concentrating on the essence of our resources in the development of new products. Our philosophy today is to grow, not to hunt," he said. Last year the company bought Fisons of Britain.
He dismissed rumours Rhone-Poulenc wanted to merge its drugs unit with either Elf-Aquitaine unit Sanofi or Synthelabo.
"As far as we are concerned, our aim is not to marry but to do the most we can with the products we have in the pipeline," he said.

Between now and the year 2000, Rhone-Poulenc Rorer will have 18 of these new products out on the market. They will add about $2.0 billion to group sales. The contribution of there products will triple to reach some 30 percent of total sales in 2000 and 50 percent in 2005 against 10 percent in 1995.

Among them are recent blockbusters such as Taxotere (cancer-treatment), Lovenox/Clexane (thrombosis) and Synercid (anti-inflammatory) which on their own will make up 50 percent of the two billion in sales by the new products.
The other products are still in approval stages such as Campto, Rilutek, Zagram, Kestine and Menorest.
New applications are expected for Lovenox, Dilaco RX, Nasacort AQ and DDAVP.
Since 1992, Rhone-Poulenc Rorer has reduced product portfolio under development to 26 from 50 in order to speed up the global registration process.
De Rosen said that other priorities were to build up the group's presence in the world, mainly in the U.S., Japan and southeast Asia.
Rhone-Poulenc Rorer wants to improve its cost structure by cutting sales costs to 34 percent of sales by 2000 from 38.5 percent in 1995.
In Paris, Rhone-Poulenc shares rose one franc or 0.72 percent to 139.40. Rhone-Poulenc Rorer closed in Paris 5.2 francs lower at 385 franc. In New York it was trading 3/8 down at 74-1/2 at 1604 GMT.
